verdict.rationale: The evidence shows no built-in natural-language assistant for building or operating n8n itself. The closest support is indirect. The documented MCP Server Trigger can expose workflows as tools that an external AI client can call through natural-language prompts. Users can also build their own AI-agent workflows, and the site markets a 'convert natural language into API calls' use case. Missing for 10: a first-party natural-language interface for creating, editing and running workflows, documentation that the MCP or agent route covers managing the product rather than only invoking workflows, and hands-on or independent corroboration.
